where_to_apply.authority: Embassy of Japan in the UK

steps.title: Confirm eVISA eligibility
steps.action: Open the Embassy’s eVISA page and confirm that you meet its UK-residence-permission requirement and that your tourism stay will be less than 90 days before starting the online route.
steps.timing: Before preparing or starting the application.

steps.title: Gather checklist documents
steps.action: Read and gather the items on the Embassy’s official Temporary Visitor Visa tourism checklist. Do not submit an application more than three months before your planned arrival in Japan.
steps.timing: Before logging in to apply; no more than three months before arrival.

steps.title: Submit online application
steps.action: Use the Embassy’s eVISA route to enter the required application information and upload the required documents. The Embassy recommends applying about two months before planned travel and allowing two to three weeks for processing.
steps.timing: About two months before travel; allow two to three weeks.

steps.title: Check result and pay
steps.action: Monitor the registered email address for the application result and any payment instructions. If payment applies, register credit or debit card details on the designated website; the Embassy says payment processing takes one working day after card details are registered. The eVISA is issued after the stated payment or,
steps.timing: After the result notification and any payment instruction.

where_to_apply.authority: Embassy of Japan in the UK
where_to_apply.application_method: Online eVISA, if you have permission to reside in the UK and meet the stated tourism and stay-length conditions

steps.title: Confirm eVISA eligibility
steps.action: Open the Embassy’s eVISA page and confirm that you have permission to reside in the UK, are travelling for tourism, and will stay for less than 90 days. If your trip includes visiting acquaintances or relatives, or business or academic activities, the page says an eVISA cannot be used and you should book an in-person E
steps.timing: Before starting an application; the Embassy recommends applying about two months before travel.

steps.title: Read the tourism checklist
steps.action: Gather the materials specified on the Embassy’s official Temporary Visitor Visa tourism checklist before logging in or starting an application.

steps.title: Submit eVISA information
steps.action: If eligible for eVISA, enter the required information in the online visa application and upload the required materials. The Embassy warns that incorrect information or inadequate uploads can delay assessment or lead to cancellation.
steps.timing: After document preparation; allow 2–3 weeks for processing.

steps.title: Watch for the result
steps.action: Check the registered email address for the visa result and, if applicable, payment instructions.
steps.timing: After submitting the application; processing normally averages about two weeks.

steps.title: Complete payment if instructed
steps.action: If payment is applicable, register credit or debit card details on the designated website. The Embassy states that full payment takes one working day to process after card registration.

steps.title: Wait for eVISA issuance
steps.action: For an application that incurs a fee, wait for payment-card verification and eVISA issuance; for one that does not incur a fee, issuance follows the result notification.
steps.timing: After the result notification and, where applicable, payment processing.

unresolved: Do you have permission to reside in the UK? The Embassy’s eVISA route requires this, but the profile does not record your UK immigration status.

If you are not eligible for eVISA, confirm with the Embassy how to book the stated in-person appointment and what submission process applies; the supplied pages do not provide those operational details.

where_to_apply.authority: Embassy of Japan in the UK
where_to_apply.application_method: Online eVISA application for eligible tourism applicants

steps.title: Confirm eVISA eligibility
steps.action: Open the Embassy of Japan in the UK eVISA page and confirm that you meet its tourism, UK-residence-permission, and stay-length conditions before using the online route. If you cannot confirm eligibility, contact the published Japan Visa Information Hotline or the Embassy for the applicable route.

steps.title: Read the official checklist
steps.action: Gather the materials specified in the Embassy’s official Temporary Visitor Visa tourism checklist; do not submit an application more than three months before your planned arrival.
steps.timing: Before logging in to the eVISA application; no earlier than three months before arrival.

steps.title: Submit the online application
steps.action: After preparing the checklist materials, enter the required information in the online visa application and upload the required materials. Check entries and uploads carefully because the Embassy says incorrect or inadequate submissions can delay assessment or lead to cancellation.
steps.timing: The Embassy recommends applying about two months before planned travel and allowing two to three weeks for processing.

steps.title: Watch for the result
steps.action: Monitor the registered email address for the application result and any payment instructions.
steps.timing: After submission; the Embassy says tourism eVISA processing normally averages about two weeks.

steps.title: Complete payment if instructed
steps.action: If payment is applicable, register credit or debit card details on the designated website as instructed in the result notification. The Embassy says payment processing takes one working day after card details are registered.

steps.title: Receive the eVISA
steps.action: Wait for eVISA issuance after the result and, where applicable, payment verification. Issuance is conditional on the application being approved.
steps.timing: After the result notification and any applicable payment processing.

where_to_apply.authority: Embassy of Japan in the UK
where_to_apply.application_method: Online eVISA application, if you meet the stated UK-residence-permission eligibility condition

steps.title: Confirm eVISA eligibility
steps.action: Open the Embassy’s eVISA page and confirm whether you meet its condition of having permission to reside in the UK for a tourism visit of less than 90 days.
steps.timing: Before choosing the online route or starting an application.

steps.title: Read the official checklist
steps.action: Gather the items on the Embassy’s official Temporary Visitor Visa tourism checklist before starting the application. Do not apply more than three months before planned arrival.
steps.timing: Before starting the application; the Embassy says applications cannot be accepted more than three months before arrival.

steps.title: Submit the eVISA application
steps.action: If you confirm eVISA eligibility, use the Embassy’s linked Ministry of Foreign Affairs online application route to enter the required information and upload the required material. The Embassy states that an in-person appointment is not required for the eVISA route.
steps.timing: The Embassy recommends applying about two months before travel and allowing two to three weeks for processing.

steps.title: Monitor the result email
steps.action: Check the registered email address for the application result and any payment instructions. If payment is applicable, follow the designated payment instructions after receiving them.
steps.timing: After submission; the Embassy describes average processing as about two weeks.

steps.title: Wait for eVISA issuance
steps.action: If the application is approved, wait for eVISA issuance after the stated result and, where applicable, payment process. Do not treat an application or visa as a guarantee of entry; landing permission is decided at the port of entry.
steps.timing: After the result notification and any applicable payment; payment-card verification is stated to take one working day.

unresolved: Do you have permission to reside in the UK? This is a stated eligibility condition for the Embassy’s tourism eVISA route; if not, the readable sources do not establish the application route for you.
The eVISA page says “no fee,” while the Embassy’s visa-fee page lists a £4.00 single-entry visa fee for Indian nationals. Confirm with the Embassy which fee, if any, applies to your selected route.

If you are not eligible for the eVISA route, confirm directly with the Embassy of Japan in the UK how and where to submit a Temporary Visitor Visa application; the readable checklist does not state the submission method or attendance requirement for that alternative route.
